raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
**Validation status: Three interleaved H20×8 Qwen3.5 MTP baseline/patch pairs completed on the exact current PR head (`2557998e0a`). All six runs reached Ready and passed a limited serving smoke check. Engine-start → Kubernetes Ready showed no measurable improvement; non-Qwen GPU and model-accuracy validation remain pending.**

Current commit: `2557998e0a29ef83522b648d8182dab3eb77d937` (base `bd2d73daa5`). The separate RunAI integration is #43255 and depends on this PR. The focused tests below were rerun after this rebase.

## Motivation

Refs #43196. MTP workers load a main model and a draft, but rejecting unused checkpoint tensors inside `load_weights` is too late to keep an earlier reader or prefetcher from touching unnecessary shards.

Inspired by [vLLM #60152](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60152), this change lets each model declare which raw checkpoint names it cannot use. The model's existing load loop and the generic file selector use the same rule. The generic loader does not assume an `mtp.` prefix.

Related SGLang proposals #35395 and #39365 also select Default-loader shards. This approach differs by sharing each model's existing role-selection rule with its actual load loop, covering multiple architecture families and exposing the same optional contract for the separate RunAI integration. The maintainers should decide whether these approaches should converge before merge.

## Modifications

- Add the optional, instance-bound `is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name)` contract. `True` means the model can definitely skip that raw checkpoint name; a missing hook preserves existing behavior.
- Extract role-selection predicates from Qwen3.5/Qwen3-Next and DeepSeek/GLM NextN loading rules. Preserve Qwen3.5 draft PP embedding requirements, NextN layer selection, and shared-weight exclusions. Leave tensor renaming, quantization, fusion and assignment in their existing model loaders.
- Select complete local safetensors files before both ordinary Default iteration and startup prefetch. Keep any file with at least one potentially required tensor, preserve order and retain the existing all-rejected fallback.
- Leave unsupported name transformations and non-safetensors loading on their original paths. Opt out wrappers whose inherited predicate does not describe their raw checkpoint namespace.

This is file-level selection, not tensor/range-level I/O. Mixed shards can still be read by both roles. Hugging Face files resolved to local storage may already have been downloaded; local read reduction is not a claim of reduced HF download traffic. No RunAI, ModelExpress P2P, model forward or scheduler behavior is added by this commit.

The cost depends on the reader: ordinary mmap without prefetch does not necessarily read all unused tensor payloads. Disabling mmap, enabling checkpoint prefetch, or using fastsafetensors has different read/transfer behavior. Benchmarks will report those settings separately; Default results cannot be inferred from RunAI measurements.

## Accuracy Tests

At the current Default-only commit, focused loader/prefetch/model-rule and affected model/quantization regressions completed with **67 passed, 152 subtests passed, 7 warnings**. Changed-file pre-commit hooks also passed after the rebase. Tests cover real tiny safetensors files, selection before iterator/prefetch, PP embeddings, role-specific NextN rules and name-domain fallbacks. The CPU backend warnings are retained in the raw log.

On the exact current head, three Qwen3.5 patch Pods and three matching baseline Pods reached Kubernetes Ready with zero engine restarts. Each returned HTTP 200 for a fixed four-output batch (64 tokens per output); draft counters recorded 1 accepted / 251 proposed in each batch. This confirms limited execution of the serving and draft paths, **not** semantic accuracy or speculative-decoding quality. Non-Qwen GPU validation remains pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Verdict: no measurable end-to-end Ready improvement in three interleaved pairs.** The baseline was upstream `bd2d73daa5` (image digest `ff746b2509f2`); the patch was this PR's exact head `2557998e0a` (image digest `a1fb6390d513`). All six archived engine logs report these build commits. The Pods used the same H20×8 node, Qwen3.5 MTP 122B checkpoint, launch flags, resource requests and resolved Pod spec apart from image/name/arm label. The primary interval is engine-container `startedAt` → Kubernetes Ready; checkpoint preparation/init, scheduling and image pull are excluded. TP0 load intervals are nested observations, not additive components of that total.

| Interleaved pair | Baseline Ready | Patch Ready | Patch − baseline | TP0 draft load, baseline → patch |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 (baseline → patch) | 333 s | 334 s | +1 s | 2.67 → 0.97 s |
| 2 (patch → baseline) | 338 s | 333 s | −5 s | 2.37 → 1.00 s |
| 3 (baseline → patch) | 336 s | 336 s | 0 s | 2.40 → 1.00 s |

The **paired Ready difference has median 0 s, range −5 to +1 s**; the gap is smaller than run-to-run variation. TP0 draft-load median was 2.40 → 1.00 s in these runs, while main load was about 89–93 s and the observed Graph prefill/target-verify windows were about 61/78–79 s. No profiler established a single overall limiter. Baseline local-shard iterators consumed 49/49 main and 49/49 draft files; patch consumed 49/49 main and 1/1 draft file. Iterator counts are not measured bytes. All six runs were Ready with zero restarts and the fixed HTTP-200 batch described above.

The checkpoint was staged in each Pod's fresh local `emptyDir` before the engine interval. Host page cache and node load were not controlled, and actual disk or object-store read bytes were not measured. This supports a narrower draft-load observation, **not** a stable startup speedup or reduced checkpoint-download claim. Three of five planned pairs are complete; two remain. A separate non-Qwen GPU run is also pending.

A fixed-revision checkpoint-index audit using the production model hooks gives:

| Checkpoint | Main files selected | Draft files selected |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.5-27B | 11/11 | 5/11 |
| GLM-4.7-Flash | 47/48 | 1/48 |

This checks rule coverage across two model families. It is **not** a measurement of bytes read, host-page-cache misses, or startup time; mixed files can be selected for both roles.

## Reviewer focus

The intended boundary is: each model owns the raw-name rule used by its existing `load_weights` loop; the generic Default loader only maps that rule to whole-file selection **before** iterator/prefetch creation. Please pay particular attention to Qwen3.5 pipeline-parallel embeddings, DeepSeek/GLM NextN shared weights, mixed shards, and the conservative fallback when a name transformation is not understood. This is deliberately distinct from RunAI in #43255 and from vLLM's [Default PR #60152](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60152) / [RunAI PR #60759](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60759).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Targeted isort/Ruff/registered-test checks passed; this is not a claim that every repository hook or GPU CI suite passed. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation preparation.

## Review and Merge Process

Design/code review is welcome now. The exact-head Qwen3.5 GPU pairs establish a limited serving smoke check and an inconclusive Ready-time result; non-Qwen GPU correctness, accuracy, read-traffic measurement and the remaining repeated pairs are still open before any broader merge/performance claim.

The red GitHub PR-test summaries on this head are opt-in gate failures, not executed model-loader test failures: the `pr-gate` job reports a missing `run-ci` label, and downstream test jobs were skipped. Repository policy requires an authorized CI trigger; the local/GPU results above do not substitute for that upstream CI.

Hi @b8zhong and @mmangkad — could you review the model-owned MTP weight-selection contract and Default/prefetch integration in this PR? The description now reflects the current post-rebase commit, the Qwen/DeepSeek/GLM rule coverage, conservative fallbacks, and the focused CPU regression results. The separate RunAI integration is stacked in #43255.

Paired GPU correctness and startup-performance measurements are still in progress; I am requesting design/code feedback now, not claiming a measured GPU speedup or asking for merge approval yet. Thank you!

+"""Model-owned MTP checkpoint selection, without allocating model weights."""
+
+import unittest

+def _without_weights(model_class, **config):
+    model = model_class.__new__(model_class)
+    torch.nn.Module.__init__(model)
+    model.config = SimpleNamespace(**config)
+    return model
+
+
+class TestQwenCheckpointSelection(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_different_subclass_layout_does_not_inherit_qwen_filter(self):
+        from sglang.srt.models.interns2_mobius import (
+            InternS2MobiusForConditionalGeneration,
+        )
+
+        model = _without_weights(InternS2MobiusForConditionalGeneration)
+        self.assertIsNone(getattr(model, "is_unused_checkpoint_weight", None))
+
+    def test_qwen35_main_and_draft_use_distinct_rules(self):
+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5 import (
+            Qwen3_5ForCausalLM,
+            Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration,
+            Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM,
+            Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration,
+        )
+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5_mtp import Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP
+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5_text import (
+            Qwen3_5ForCausalLM as Qwen3_5TextForCausalLM,
+        )
+
+        cases = [
+            ("model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight", False, True),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight", True, False),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.up_proj.weight_scale", True, False),
+            ("mtp.fc.weight", True, False),
+            ("model.embed_tokens.weight", False, False),
+            ("model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight", False, False),
+            ("lm_head.weight", False, True),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.rotary_emb.inv_freq", True, True),
+        ]
+        for cls in (
+            Qwen3_5ForCausalLM,
+            Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration,
+            Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM,
+            Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration,
+            Qwen3_5TextForCausalLM,
+        ):
+            main = _without_weights(cls)
+            draft = _without_weights(Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP)
+            for name, main_unused, draft_unused in cases:
+                with self.subTest(model=cls.__name__, name=name):
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        main.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name), main_unused
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        draft.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name), draft_unused
+                    )
+

+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_next import Qwen3NextForCausalLM
+        from sglang.srt.models.qwen3_next_mtp import Qwen3NextForCausalLMMTP
+
+        main = _without_weights(Qwen3NextForCausalLM)
+        draft = _without_weights(Qwen3NextForCausalLMMTP)
+        for name, main_unused, draft_unused in (
+            ("model.embed_tokens.weight", False, True),
+            ("model.layers.0.mlp.up_proj.weight", False, True),
+            ("mtp.pre_fc_norm_embedding.weight", True, False),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.mlp.up_proj.weight_scale", True, False),
+            ("mtp.layers.0.rotary_emb.inv_freq", True, True),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(name=name):
+                self.assertEqual(main.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name), main_unused)
+                self.assertEqual(draft.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name), draft_unused)
+

+                    prefix + "shared_head.head.weight",
+                    prefix + "embed_tokens.weight",
+                ):
+                    with self.subTest(model=draft_cls.__name__, name=name):
+                        self.assertTrue(draft.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name))
+                self.assertFalse(
+                    main.is_unused_checkpoint_weight("model.layers.0.mlp.weight")
+                )
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    main.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(
+                        f"model.layers.{num_layers}.eh_proj.weight"
+                    )
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
